Prisma schema separately persists messages and versions; selection, preview and download all read the chosen durable version (articulation 8).

OpenAI returns a structured multi-page React graph with editable element IDs and navigation (ai_in_loop 8, authority 8). An AI editElement method exists but the exposed edit route does not call it; visual edits are deterministic overlays, so the record's own AI does not mutate the graph (mutation 3). Page/overlay maps are server-memory only and vanish on restart (articulation 4).

Stage-wise Gemini calls produce master plan, design document, CSS and section templates that feed later stages (ai_in_loop 7, authority 7). No correction loop at this commit; generation is one-shot from a brief (mutation 2). Builder writes plan/design records and materializes a website directory, a durable but unversioned output (articulation 6).

OpenAI completion with labelled HTML/CSS/JS sections is parsed into three mutable source strings (ai_in_loop 7, authority 7). The model determines the artifact but the parser is fragile; strings are user-editable in the browser and there is no model-driven correction of existing work (mutation 3). Same state feeds iframe proof and ZIP of three files; no project database (articulation 5).

Local Llama 3 via Ollama returns JSON HTML/CSS/JS assigned to a sandbox iframe (ai_in_loop 7, authority 7). One-shot raw message with no validation; no export, correction or recovery path, and values exist only for the page session (mutation 2, articulation 3).

Gemini writes a self-contained HTML/CSS/JS page under a simple contract; markdown fences stripped but no schema layer (ai_in_loop 7, authority 7). Fixed filenames overwritten each run with no correction loop, so AI never edits existing work (mutation 2). index.html and website.zip are produced for preview/download but without session isolation or version recovery (articulation 5).

TinyLlama extracts a bounded schema (site type, theme, metadata, components); deterministic templates select known HTML sections and colors (ai_in_loop 6, authority 5). No correction protocol or history; invalid schema falls back (mutation 2). Projected HTML/CSS retained for separate downloads only, no durable store (articulation 5).

Gemini authors a single self-contained HTML document; improvement route receives current code and returns a complete replacement (ai_in_loop 8, authority 8). Refinement is whole-document regeneration of the existing value, a real AI iteration loop although not patch-level (mutation 6). One code state in browser across Monaco/iframe/download with no database or reload path (articulation 5).

ChatGPT writes page HTML while Stable Horde supplies imagery, coordinated server-side (ai_in_loop 7, authority 7). No local revision graph; github_utils updates the GitHub representation for deployment, which is delivery rather than AI design mutation (mutation 2). Deployable page via GitHub/Vercel is a durable external artifact (articulation 6); historical since 2023.

Groq returns typed html/css/js fields shown as editable textareas and composed into an iframe (ai_in_loop 7, authority 7). Regeneration replaces the current object in place without snapshots, undo or model-driven repair of existing work (mutation 3). Copy/ZIP export preserves work but an unused DB scaffold means no durable projects (articulation 5).

Gemini via LangChain returns delimited HTML/CSS/JS that is extracted and concatenated for preview (ai_in_loop 7, authority 7). No correction or version path; generation is one-shot (mutation 2). Files are written and zipped as a transient delivery stage with no saved project (articulation 5).

Gemini generates the site through a configured service inside a Laravel controller (ai_in_loop 7, authority 7). Create-or-retrieve generation with no correction or branching revision graph, so the model does not edit existing records (mutation 2). GeneratedWebsite model durably retains intent and artifact in the database (articulation 7).

Local Qwen returns three fenced code blocks parsed into fields kept in React state (ai_in_loop 7, authority 7). No correction loop, history or recovery; generation is one-shot (mutation 2). Preview and ZIP share current values as export artifacts, but nothing is persisted (articulation 5).

Puter AI returns strict JSON HTML/CSS/JS with multi-strategy parsing (ai_in_loop 7); an explicit fixed fallback bundle means the visible artifact is not always model-authored, so authority is capped (authority 6). No model-driven editing of saved projects (mutation 2). Bundles persist as MongoDB projects with create/list/get/delete and reload, though unversioned (articulation 7).

Three grounding modes (brief, screenshot, Figma context) converge on Groq-generated website code (ai_in_loop 7, authority 7). Input adapters feed generation but the model never edits existing source; acceptance is followed by Netlify deployment (mutation 2). Deployed source is a durable delivery artifact, with browser review before release (articulation 6).

Four provider families sit behind one interface and their answers are parsed/schema-assembled into a structured website project rather than raw chat text (ai_in_loop 8, authority 7). No evidence of AI-driven editing of existing projects (mutation 3). Server storage persists the structured project with preview/code/download views but no branch-oriented version graph (articulation 7).

LangChain Gemini chain returns HTML/CSS/JS separated and rendered live (ai_in_loop 7, authority 7). Streamlit session owns only the current result with no correction or version loop (mutation 2). Downloadable output but no durable project or version database (articulation 5).

Four provider families support both generation and modification of a site, normalized onto one browser-side artifact (ai_in_loop 8, authority 8). Model outputs accumulate in versionHistory and can be seeded from imports, so AI modifies existing source snapshots within the session (mutation 7). Version comparison, revert and ZIP delivery exist but history is browser-memory, not durable (articulation 6).

Chat route streams agent output into an in-memory file set mounted and started in a WebContainer; generated files and running app are views of the same set (ai_in_loop 8, authority 8). Subsequent chat regenerates/updates that file set, so the model iterates on existing files (mutation 6). Editor plus running preview constitute a real workspace, but it is in-memory with no server-side projects or recovery (articulation 6).

Two-stage loop: Groq first expands the brief with concrete visual decisions, then Groq/HF/OpenRouter generate the final HTML (ai_in_loop 9, authority 8). Saving promotes transient output to one MongoDB snapshot; model does not iterate on the saved project (mutation 4). Brief, enhanced brief, analysis and HTML persist in a durable record with real provider deploy routes (articulation 7); not a version graph.

Gemini emits a validated WebsiteBlueprint (type, theme, sections, colors, content) with retry/normalization (ai_in_loop 8). Fixed Python renderers retain rendering authority, so the model fills content/composition but deterministic code authors the markup (authority 6). No correction loop; compiled HTML and blueprint/prompt persist in MongoDB and disk (mutation 2, articulation 7).

Prompt-based generation and edits replace entries in the backend's page map (ai_in_loop 7, authority 7). AI edits do mutate the server-side current map, but the map is process-memory and vanishes on restart (mutation 6, articulation 3); manual editor changes live in component state with no merge/save protocol and preview is the only end of the loop.

The product is a human-authored DAG executed by a real multi-handler runtime; a local Qwen LLM call is one node type producing outputs inside runs (ai_in_loop 5). The AI does not design or mutate the workflow graph (authority 2, mutation 2). PostgreSQL persists workflows/nodes/edges/runs/per-node executions durably (articulation 7).

Workflow authoring is human composition of typed steps/triggers; an LLM step executes within runs but does not take design decisions (ai_in_loop 5). AI neither creates nor edits the workflow (authority 2, mutation 2). Nhost relational rows for workflows, steps, triggers and runs with tenant RBAC and approval gates are durable and govern execution (articulation 8).

The record translates a human-drawn DAG into LangChain/OpenAI Python or AI SDK TypeScript; models are only invoked when the generated code runs, so the model loop belongs to generated programs, not the record's own design loop (ai_in_loop 4, authority 2, mutation 2). Generated source is the executable artifact and exports are real, but the DAG lives in an ephemeral client store with no durable project repo (articulation 5).

Real graph-to-Gemini loop: the backend sends query plus document to Gemini and returns the answer (ai_in_loop 5). The graph is human-composed and the runtime ignores edges and per-node dispatch, so the AI does not design or mutate the workflow (authority 2, mutation 2). Durability is JSON import/export; PostgreSQL stores document metadata, not the graph (articulation 5).

Executor reloads a human-authored ordered workflow and calls Groq for LLM nodes, performing HTTP/DB/notification actions and persisting outputs (ai_in_loop 5). The AI does not author or edit the workflow (authority 2, mutation 2). Workflow_steps, step_runs, trigger approval and membership/quota checks are durable server-backed records that the runtime consumes (articulation 8).

Groq's Llama returns a strict workflow name/trigger/step schema that is rendered and then materialized into n8n via its API (ai_in_loop 7, authority 6 — model authors the workflow structure). It posts a new workflow rather than editing existing ones (mutation 3). The delivered n8n object is visible/durable, but every action is a noOp node with notes only, so executability and runtime evidence remain delegated to n8n (articulation 6).

A governed ordered-step console where humans configure steps; Gemini is invoked for the LLM step but with a hard-coded test prompt, so model design authority is minimal (ai_in_loop 5, authority 2, mutation 2). Hasura-backed workflows, ordered steps, persistent runs and approval resume are durable and tenant-scoped (articulation 8); several action types remain simulated.

Gemini proposes a six-line plan graph (trigger/action/output) parsed into connected React Flow nodes (ai_in_loop 7, authority 6). Human users move/delete/edit nodes; the AI does not edit its own plan (mutation 2). Plan exists only in client state with no save/load/export, and edges do not drive execution (articulation 3).

Human-composed ordered workflow triggers real Groq or HTTP calls and approval gates pause/resume runs (ai_in_loop 5). The AI neither designs nor mutates the workflow (authority 2, mutation 2). Hasura GraphQL persists workflows, ordered steps, triggers, runs and per-step status with quota/role governance (articulation 8); branch semantics and some effects are synthetic.

Saved blocks/connections are consumed by the execute route, which invokes the Vercel AI SDK for supported block types (ai_in_loop 5). AI chat can describe suggested workflow JSON but does not parse into the canvas, so AI never designs or edits the graph (authority 2, mutation 2). Workflows, blocks, connections, runs and per-block outcomes are persisted durably (articulation 7).

Vue Flow editor writes relational records consumed by FastAPI, which performs HTTP/LiteLLM calls following the first outgoing connection (ai_in_loop 5). The AI executes within a human-authored linear path and never edits the graph (authority 2, mutation 2). Flows, steps and connections persist and runs return collected outputs, though step-level history is not persisted (articulation 7).

The model streams implementation markup into the conversation and can be prompted again with history, plus a second model call translates accepted HTML to another framework (ai_in_loop 8, authority 7). AI iterates on the conversational artifact and re-processes it for export, but not on a persistent project (mutation 5). No durable store or version graph; rendered component is a projection of in-browser source (articulation 4); historical since 2024.

Saved node/edge configuration compiles into a LangGraph StateGraph with LLM/RAG/MCP/decision handlers and nested-workflow composition, so models run and their outputs drive execution (ai_in_loop 6). Agents/workflows are human-authored; the AI executes within them and does not edit the graph (authority 2, mutation 2). PostgreSQL models, versions, deployments and execution logs plus voice/WhatsApp entry points make the artifact fully operational and durable (articulation 9).

AI Layout generates multiple furniture layouts from room+constraints and AI rendering/style transfer projects the design; user selects and manually edits, so AI participates strongly in layout decisions but human gates. Mutation limited: AI produces candidate layouts and style renders into the editable project, regeneration/iteration exists but not deep repair of the spatial graph. Articulation high: canonical editable 3D room graph feeding CAD/BOM/quote and manufacturing.

Model classifies and suggests suffix-only key segments, but human confirms feature/screen anchors, reviews, edits or skips; deterministic validation and dictionary bypass constrain the model. AI authority low: anchors are human-provided and model cannot choose the whole key. AI never mutates: rename only on UI apply message for a reviewed key. Articulation strong: native Figma text node names plus a file-local common-key dictionary.

Built-in assistants create presentations/documents/spreadsheets/images/web artifacts from briefs in hosted agent sessions; native PPTX mutation lives in the separate OfficeCLI record. AI writes workspace artifacts and workspace files remain authoritative with history and direct HTML/code editing, so AI can revise existing workspace content. Articulation strong: durable workspace files with workspaceHistory and live preview routing.

No model call in the authored record: simulation and deployment advance via setTimeout/timed modal stages and never post nodes to a backend; the backend orchestrator is adjacent and not connected to the canvas. All canvas authoring is human. No AI mutation exists. Articulation decent: a genuine user-controlled graph artifact with JSON import/export and localStorage save, but runtime is a demo.

Agent workspace where a human-built graph compiles into an event-driven runtime; no direct evidence of model calls or AI design decisions in the record, workflows execute under it. Graph authoring is human; runtime executes. No evidence AI edits persistent work. Articulation strong: serialized graph models, compiler-projected runtime objects, sqlite event store with checkpoints and WAL.

Core loop streams through the AI SDK provider and persists every response as a new versioned file in a branching graph; model corrections revise existing files. AI turns prompts into complete HTML documents; user edits via Monaco join the same graph. Mutation strong: model corrections and version links on existing files in IndexedDB. Articulation strong: projects/files/versions/messages/model credentials and reusable rules are explicit versioned records.

Zero-dependency deterministic CLI engine: no model call of its own; it is a mechanism that an external AI or human uses to plan op-lists that edit .kicad_sch. Creation authority belongs to the caller. The tool itself can structurally mutate persistent schematics when invoked, but no record-owned AI. Articulation strong: versioned JSON op-lists, diffs, SARIF, SVG, atomic writes, backups and undo over a normalized model.

OVHcloud models generate and revise one complete HTML document; prompt refinement requests a replacement document from the server, and manual edits are promoted back into the transcript. AI authority high for a single-file site. Mutation exists via refinement of the existing document but is a linear replace with no branch/diff/restore. Articulation moderate: localStorage transcript is recoverable source trail, not named projects or a version graph.

Pinned implementation calls no language or image model; Perceptor/Planner/Reviewer run fixed deterministic matrices and template selection, so the core loop has no model. Creation is automated but rules-based, not AI. No AI mutation. Articulation good: multi-resolution icons, theme JSON, proposal/report JSON/Markdown with trace ID, approval record and design-decision log are durable artifacts.

Chat route streams AI SDK output that plans write/rename/delete/install operations on the WebContainer project; the model is the project's main driver. Human approval gates every operation batch, capping authority. AI mutates existing files once approved (ordered execution), but undo is session-local and incomplete. Articulation moderate: WebContainer files are the live authority but reload discards version array and durability needs export.

LLM-facing text-to-3D server and SDF runtime: design decisions come from the calling LLM; the server translates requests into scene operations and the kernel is deterministic. Per the rule for engines enabling an external agent, ai_in_loop and authority cap at 2. The record CAN create/edit persistent SDF programs when called. Articulation strong: compiled SDF instructions/constraints remain evaluable across GPU, browser and host bindings with mesh export.

Reasoning selects and reasons over component material and creator drives generated website creation; model output is persisted as Django objects with stored HTML. AI assembles pages from component material. Remix reconnects existing output to editing/regeneration, a real correction path. Articulation strong: persisted website-generation records, images, preview editor and generated-site corpus.

Browser is deliberately view-only; an external coding agent edits MDX source, so the model loop belongs to the caller while the record supplies deck rules via bundled skills. Creation by external agent. Mutation medium: the platform is explicitly designed for agents to continually edit MDX source with hot reload, but the AI is external. Articulation strong: per-slide MDX modules are the durable editable authority with PDF/PPTX as exports.

Multi-provider agents plan pad topology and tool actions and generate Cadence SKILL for IO-ring layout; the record itself orchestrates the model loop. AI produces layout plans/SKILL but requires a licensed Virtuoso/PDK environment to execute, and golden cases prove orchestration rather than production sign-off. Mutation via generated SKILL into Cadence objects is evidenced in benchmarks. Articulation good: io_ring_intent_graph.json is a replayable design contract plus generated SKILL and verification reports.

Scored from public contracts: p2c/l2c/f2c generation jobs turn prompts/images/URLs/Figma into a sessionId-addressed internal Git artifact; chat and agent Git clone-push edit existing artifacts, with version history, restore and duplicate. AI makes the core design decisions for artifact creation. Mutation strong: agents add/modify/delete files via chat or short-lived Git push into the live artifact. Articulation strong: Git-backed code authority, preview, version history and deployment are durable.

Agent mode revises a selected DOM element through natural language with the selected tag/text/styles/CSS path as bounded target; the agent is the deck creator and patch engine. AI writes full HTML decks and patches elements. Mutation strong: selected-DOM agent edits existing HTML with end-to-end tested version saves and restores, while GrapesJS direct edits serialize back into the same source. Articulation strong: original HTML is the durable authority with named versions.

Skill that an external agent executes: the record carries no own model call, it resolves platform/brand direction and orchestrates the bundle writer, so loop and authority belong to the caller (cap 2). Dedicated expansion path lets later changes pass through instead of regenerating, an AI-driven modification route. Articulation strong: CJX-ready multi-file HTML/CSS/JS bundle with foundation.css as token authority and asset ownership records.

Core library is deterministic once syntax/options arrive; AI generation happens through first-party skills and a host agent, so the record's own AI is absent (enabler cap 2). Editing is human-driven via the embedded editor; no evidence the library's own AI mutates. Articulation good: structured infographic options/syntax are the durable embeddable state with editable structured SVG and command history (in-memory only).

Model runs a tool loop over a bounded canvas summary and can read/inspect, draw native Excalidraw structures or patch elements by ID; the client materializes structured events into the live scene. AI creates structured DAGs/diagrams from prompt. Mutation strong: model merges, updates, connects and removes existing elements. Articulation weak: the scene is React/client session state with no durable board save, versioning or auth at the pinned revision.

Server design-agent tool contract streams AI outputs that add or update screen nodes in shared project state on an infinite canvas; continuing prompts correct earlier screens. AI generates screens from prompts. Mutation strong: tool results add/update existing screen state rather than replacing with one flattened answer. Articulation moderate: project screen-node state is the authority, but no persistence/versioning evidence is given.

Coding-agent skill that scaffolds a Next.js editor; the model call belongs to the external agent (enabler cap 2). Agent prefill is one-time scaffolding while visual refinement is user-owned. Mutation limited: the editor and JSON let AI-related changes persist back to disk via /api/project, but continuing AI edit is external. Articulation strong: app-store-screenshots.json plus content-addressed assets on disk are the authoritative durable workspace with schema migrations.

Four-skill suite (consultant, brand, PDF, PPT) run by an external agent; no own model call, loop and authority cap at 2. Skills define how the agent iterates storyboard/brand into deliverables. Articulation good: storyboard, brand-brief.md and identity.js are durable cross-renderer inputs and PPTX is an editable native graph.

Selected provider returns a constrained module which is normalized into a canonical shape, validated and rendered through the product's native runtime; provider choice does not change the artifact contract. AI creates the module. Mutation weak-medium: style edits are user-driven patches back into the same tree; AI regeneration produces a new module rather than iterating the old one. Articulation strong: modules persist on device as structured state with permission-gated runtime.

Retains Bolt's structured artifact/file-action protocol for AI generation into a WebContainer project; AI SDK drives generation and correction. AI produces multi-file apps with user inspection/editing. Mutation strong: file actions create/update project files across sessions and builds restore saved projects. Articulation strong: project code file maps and chat history persist in PostgreSQL, plus Vercel/Expo delivery, though no immutable version graph.

Model generates one self-contained HTML document and prompt refinement replaces it in the durable Supabase row. AI creates the whole app file. Mutation good: refinement edits the existing current document. Articulation moderate: durable current state with iframe/copy/download exits, but iteration history is audit-only with no code snapshots, so no version control.

Early-access product claim: natural-language requirements become a feature/constraint-bearing parametric model with physics/DFM checks, but no source, benchmarks or solver internals are public; unproven dimensions kept low. Authority is claimed text-to-parametric-model. Iteration via prompt changes is claimed but not verified. Articulation medium: claimed parametric CAD model exported to STEP/IGES/STL/native formats, not source-inspected.

AI path analyzes the application-portfolio model and formulates candidate architectures or recommendations; models clearly drive proposal generation. Authority gated: proposals enter Architecture Review Board workflows rather than overwriting approved state. Mutation limited: AI does not silently write; changes flow through human review. Articulation strong: applications/capabilities/dependencies and governance metadata are first-class durable records and diagrams are views.

OpenAI-backed routes generate an architecture, reconstruct one from an image, repair invalid structure, explain and populate descriptions; the model is the authoring engine for the WAM graph. AI materializes graph content into the editor. Mutation good: the repair route edits invalid structure and regeneration inserts graph material. Articulation strong: WAM graph persisted behind authenticated projects in MongoDB with editable routed edges and validation.

Skill contract for an external agent to author typed semantic JSON; no own model call, so loop and authority cap at 2. Delta artifacts make architectural change reviewable, an AI-driven revision route executed by the caller. Articulation strong: semantic IR is validated before multi-surface delivery (HTML/PNG/SVG/WebM/cards), with delta and visual-check artifacts as durable records.

Model produces constrained JSON of components/connections that is parsed into node/edge objects and projected onto an editable canvas; brief-to-graph control path is the core loop. AI creates the graph from a brief. Mutation medium: validation/fallback sits between model and canvas; user repositions afterwards and regeneration can revise, but no evidence of deep AI iteration on existing graphs. Articulation good: the editable graph is the working authority with rendered diagram as a view.

AI is a mutation route into a typed schema graph in a Rust/Leptos app; AI actions are converted into graph operations subject to the same constraints as direct manipulation. Authority is shared with human editing of the schema. Mutation good: AI operations alter tables/columns/keys/relationships in the persistent model, human-inspectable. Articulation strong: schema graph, SQL DDL mode, CRDT LiveShare and snapshots provide mergeable durable state.

Auto mode uses parameters and generative assistance to create or regenerate building/floor/parking/site layouts in a hosted BIM project; the AI drives variant creation. Human manual mode and readonly mode gate authority; AI assistance is one of three modes. Mutation medium: regenerate parameterized solutions updates the same project with invalidation rules for stale exports. Articulation strong: navigable 3D BIM model with linked analytical metrics and IFC/DXF/XLSX delivery.

AI composes typed multi-mutation plans over the ArchitectureGraph from intent; dry-run with deterministic validation and impact comparison precedes approval. Authority gated: human approval is required before the atomic executor applies any plan, so AI has proposal not write authority. Mutation medium: approved plans apply to the persistent graph but are fully human-gated. Articulation strong: graph snapshots, actor-labelled event stream, ADR drafts and workspace persistence (localStorage).

Raw MCP server exposing thirteen operations over draw.io mxGraph XML: it enables an external agent, so loop and authority cap at 2. The server itself implements real mutation of persistent .drawio XML when invoked. Articulation good: .drawio XML files remain the durable source-control-friendly native artifact with verifier/parser tests guarding output.

Workflow control plane that coordinates AI coding agents: it runs nodes in isolated worktrees with gates and artifacts but itself holds no model loop for design decisions; agents under it do the creative work. Authority belongs to the governed agents. Mutation medium: the plane semantically manages agent-driven repository changes with isolation, events and resume paths. Articulation strong: YAML workflow definitions, event records, logs and artifact summaries are durable editable state.

Packaged extension/CLI governing external AI coding agents: DESIGN.md is the declared visual source of truth and headless-browser QA gates changes, but intelligence is the agents'; architecture-level evidence only (VSIX, no unpacked source). Authority is the agents'. Mutation via checkpoints/ship pipeline is agent-executed. Articulation good: DESIGN.md, truth-layer file, checkpoints, changelog and PR records are durable documented artifacts.

Plugin/skill suite for an external agent to produce architecture artifacts; no own model call, so loop and authority cap at 2. Commands and hooks route creation and stale-artifact warnings through the agent. Articulation strong: numbered Markdown artifacts linked by identifiers and review states over Git, with Mermaid/PlantUML diagrams and OKF import/export preserving provenance.

URL/screenshot/prompt-to-React generation with sandbox preview; AI streamed changes and visual-editor changes produce next builds in a durable build lineage. AI creates apps and iterates on existing builds. Mutation strong: builds resume sandboxes, apply AI changes and record version history. Articulation strong: persisted projects/builds/messages in the API, deployment history with rollback as a second ledger.

Four Gemini roles plan/generate/validate/explain components with explicit mock-mode provenance when the model is unavailable; generation is model-driven. AI produces component code. Mutation medium: browser history loads generated states back into the editor and manual changes affect current source, but no account-backed server versioning or archive. Articulation moderate: current source in editor with Babel-compiled live preview and copy/download.

Agentic AI expands moodboard and concept candidates across the collection lifecycle; the AI's role is candidate generation. Designers decide which direction becomes CAD/tech pack, so authority is human-gated. No public evidence AI edits technical artifacts directly. Articulation medium: collection workflow links moodboards, designs, prints, CADs and technical packs, but the data model and transfer semantics are not public.

No model call: humans arrange components into ASCII scenes and export Markdown as context for an external coding agent; the AI-native boundary is a documented handoff contract only. All creation is manual. No AI mutation. Articulation moderate: ASCII scene in local browser state with localStorage autosave and Markdown export, no backend or Git integration.

Astron Agent assists composing RPA workflows from a 300+ deterministic activity catalog and can invoke/trigger flows via conversational and MCP interfaces; AI helps design workflows over concrete capabilities. The editor owns ordering/branches/loops, so authority is shared. Mutation good: agent-designed flows are editable and debuggable after generation. Articulation strong: durable workflow definitions with step execution, logs, breakpoints and packaged deployment.

Agent team/skill pack executed by an external agent: no own model call in the record, loop and authority cap at 2. Skills direct 3D work inside Blender/Unity/Omniverse/VRoid, but mutation is agent-performed. Articulation moderate: host-native files remain authoritative and there is no independent scene runtime or cross-host persistence; team log records tool use.

Agent team/skill pack for external agents: no own model call, loop and authority cap at 2. Skills specify research, UX, UI, wireframing and prototyping to be executed in external hosts. Articulation weak: Figma/Sketch/XD/code artifacts stay in external hosts; Atlas supplies only the operating contract, commands and a local team log/audit trail.

Prompt-to-component Figma plugin: its core contract is model-driven generation of a UI component inside Figma. Architecture-level only, no public source: property/variant/auto-layout construction and whether generation modifies existing components are unproven, so authority is capped and mutation is weak. Generated component is an editable Figma artifact (articulation high).

Desktop agent product with own Copilot OAuth+PKCE model path; user requests prototypes/decks/docs and the agent creates HTML/JSX/PPTX/PDF beside DESIGN.md. Model-driven loop with workspace-attached session history. AI creates artifacts from intent, iterates on prior workspace state (moderate evidence), and output is durable editable files on disk (high articulation).

Backend LLM/agent nodes do call Gemini when configured (own loop inside node execution), but the design authority is the human-drawn LiteGraph graph; AI only fills node execution. No evidence AI edits the persisted graph JSON; mock fallback means observed runs may be simulated. JSON persistence is durable and editable.

Gated design-to-code pipeline: Figma/intent becomes spec+token lock, tests before implementation, up to five visual-diff iterations and repair against the running app. Core loop is model-driven design decision-making; AI creates the implementation and iteratively repairs it against the design. Repository source and token lock are authoritative, durable artifacts.

Agent-orchestrated project IDE: conductor runs real CLI agents that change SQLite project-management state and filesystem artifacts (Markdown, Mermaid, Obsidian canvas, Excalidraw) with structured satisfaction gating. AI agents make and act on design decisions and directly mutate persistent work. Durable via SQLite, files and Git.

Skill/workflow mechanism (SKILL.md + scripts) executed by an external agent: the model loop belongs to the caller, so ai_in_loop and authority are capped at 2. The workflow guides writing site source and gate/repair steps, and output is durable repository artifacts (site source, retained design evidence).

Document-native visual: generation route calls Anthropic to produce a tldraw snapshot embedded as an atomic TipTap node with bounded manuscript context; application code validates and owns the scene contract. AI creates a new diagram per request; no evidence AI edits existing diagrams (mutation moderate). Artifact is durable TipTap JSON saved to Convex, editable in place.

Complete model-driven paper-to-presentation pipeline: content extraction, presentation-plan JSON, LaTeX generation, compile validation with repair loop writing back to source, and revision generator consuming previous plan+TeX+feedback. Mutates the persistent LaTeX/plan authority directly. Highly durable editable artifacts.

RL policy is the record's own model loop: it chooses analog-device parameter moves that change the authoritative parameter vector, with SPICE reward closing the loop. AI directly mutates the persistent design state across iterations. Research code: YAML specs/netlists are durable but no user-facing versioning; no production canvas.

Closed commercial product scored from public contracts: AI reconstructs editable 3D scenes/characters/worlds/camera from footage/text/image and renders cinematic shots; users retain editable camera/plates/passes. Mutation within the 3D editor is strong; no established round trip from downstream DCC back. Structured USD exports and editable scene are durable.

Built-in 15-tool design loop calls providers and turns model output into typed EditorCommand mutations on the canonical PenDocument; every AI write applies via the same command boundary as human edits. Orchestrator plans/scaffolds/sections, runs isolated concurrent workers replayed deterministically, then validates; batch_design scripts are constrained and transactional. AI directly edits, repairs and iterates the persistent .op document (atomic save, 100-entry undo, collaboration protocol, Git merge with node-level resolution). Durable canonical JSON document with node identity, conversion ledger, codegen targets, and four distinct history layers.

Claude Code environment: the model loop that decides dimensions/topology belongs to the external Claude Code agent the record enables, so per the critical rule ai_in_loop and authority are capped. The encoded loop is strong at mutation: numbered .scad revisions are written to disk, rendered to PNG for visual comparison, and the user/agent refine existing versions; STL export is geometry-validated. Versioned OpenSCAD source is the durable editable authority with render/export as downstream projections.

Own multi-agent pipeline: a design agent defines parts and world-space bounding-box contracts, part agents implement them in parallel, and a vision judge sends failures back into the source, so the model loop decides the 3D structure and iterates. Blender materializes/render and topos inspect (box measurement, floating/overlap detection) ground the loop. Recoverable authority is code/outputs/<slug>/src (design.json, per-part builders, assembly, joints) while renders/GLB/URDF are disposable projections; stateless runtime enables parallel part work.

Record's own loop: LLM streams OpenUI Lang built from the registered component library, so the model composes declared vocabulary into an executable program; the runtime executes state changes and mutations without another model call. Authority is bounded by the registered component contract; incremental editing changes parts of the program rather than whole blobs, giving some AI-driven revision of generated output. Articulation is capped because OpenUI itself supplies no hosted project database/version history; durable generated programs depend on the embedding application.

Optimizely design-system implementation whose AI surface is an MCP metadata server exposing component metadata/examples plus a Proteus JSON UI spec; the record itself contains no model loop, so design decisions belong to whatever external agent calls the MCP (critical rule caps ai/authority). No evidence the AI edits existing persistent work; agents can materialize a governed Proteus artifact. Durable side is strong: typed tokens, public Proteus JSON schema, traceable component vocabulary across React/Figma with design review guarding changes.

Skill package executed by an external agent (model loop belongs to the caller), so ai_in_loop and authority are capped at 2. The encoded loop mutates persistent work: it reconstructs a 2D photonics schematic as a Blender optical table, saves/reopens the scene and runs mesh/ray/BVH/load-path checks, iterating the model with topology/aperture/load constraints as release gates. Artifacts carry manifests, hashes, annotated renders and machine-readable PASS/BLOCKED/UNVERIFIED acceptance states; result is not certification-grade.

Agent IDE whose Design Mode turns a browser selection into grounded visual evidence for the coding agents the product runs; the product orchestrates model-agent execution across isolated Git worktrees. Authority: agents implement from source-linked evidence and the user promotes chosen candidates. Mutation: agents change real repository source in worktrees, snapshotted and compared, with explicit merge/promotion so parallel AI output does not silently overwrite. Articulation: Git worktrees, snapshots, annotated diffs and CLI-controllable browser/terminal surfaces are persistent; design evidence, implementation and promotion stay separate stages.

Record's own plan route generates a structured candidate agent-and-task workflow from a project request, so the model decides the orchestration design; the run route executes tasks and the editor exposes status/logs. Authority is strong at planning but mixed with simulation-oriented status progression in delivery adapters. AI mutation of existing persistent design is limited: commit route writes accepted agent output, but the canvas graph itself is human-edited and no AI revision of the persisted graph is evidenced. Durable: workflow graph serialization, LocalStorage drafts and explicit handoff APIs.

DeepSite-lineage prompt-to-app workspace with its own model loop generating application files into a browser VFS; IndexedDB VFS (not chat text or preview DOM) is the durable local source authority. AI generates and iterates files via file tools, with checkpoints capturing restorable workspace states and ZIP/OSWS archives for portability. Execution extends the product: virtual-server serves current VFS to the preview compiler and deployments add server-managed state; independent identity beyond the DeepSite fork.

Product includes an AI assistant that proposes source/template actions, but mutating the governed DataMart requires an explicit apply gate that persists, verifies staleness and executes transactionally — so the record's own model loop makes proposals rather than autonomous design decisions. Authority: analysts own SQL; AI writes prose/reports from approved results and can create/revise reports via MCP (bounded, no arbitrary SQL). Persistent TypeORM state covers mart definitions, schemas, sessions, applied actions, reports, schedules and run history; no user-facing branch/commit history for arbitrary mart revisions.

AI boundary deliberately modest: the browser explains the schema to Claude/ChatGPT/Gemini and the user imports returned files, while the only in-record server call is a Gemini adapter generating insight questions, not design decisions — so the design-authoring loop is external and capped. Round-trip import/export between OKF Markdown bundles and the canvas lets externally authored models become editable graph state, with an explicit push gate to Data Marts drafts. Portable one-model-two-projections design (Markdown+YAML frontmatter vs. canvas) is durable and re-importable.

Record's own OpenRouter call fills a bounded SiteDraft schema (eyebrow/headline/description/CTA/features) with deterministic local fallback, so the model takes content-level design decisions while a deterministic renderer owns layout. No evidence for AI editing existing work: output is one-shot generation with no revision path. Articulation is capped: the draft renders as responsive preview and interpolates into standalone HTML export, but arbitrary layout editing and durable projects are outside the product.

Extension's Generate controller routes prompt+reference to OpenAI/Anthropic itself, so the record contains its own model call producing PageBuilder-compatible content; Magento PageBuilder owns the published page graph and the model proposes native markup/field values. Authority is bounded by the host CMS. Mutation: proposals land as drafts (queue + approval) before becoming page state; no evidence the model revises existing published pages autonomously. Durable governance: saved prompt templates, knowledge base, RequestLogger records and monthly budgets; inserted blocks editable via normal Magento operations.

Closed hosted design canvas; public evidence shows design decisions come from external Claude/Codex agents through the localhost MCP gateway and the product's own AI is limited to image/AI-agent features with no evidenced core design loop, so ai/authority are penalized per closed-product rules. Mutation is well documented: id-addressed create/move/duplicate/update_styles/write_html/delete operations mutate the currently open hosted file the user also edits. Articulation: durable URL-addressed hosted file with real-time collaboration, tokens and presence, but version history/restore/backup and MCP revision semantics are undisclosed and must be penalized.

Packaged ChatGPT workflow: the model loop that generates/scores figure candidates belongs to external ChatGPT, and the record is a prompt/architecture package — per the critical rule ai_in_loop and authority are capped. Mutation is one-shot: generated images are review candidates, not an editable graph, and there is no AI edit of existing persistent work. Articulation: prompt packages, issue ledgers and checkpoints carry a durable decision trail, but final selection and manual SVG/PowerPoint reconstruction remain human work.

Hosted commercial product (Nexus) recorded only at architecture/workflow-claims level; complete source is private and first-party explicitly distinguishes it from open Paper2Any. Model calls and generation mechanics are asserted but not source-verified, and lifecycle access was blocked, so AI-native dimensions are penalized for lack of evidence. Durable surface is only architectural: persistent Spaces, specialist Labs, online Office previews and async long-running jobs; no source-level artifact model or runtime is disclosed.

Agent-skill workspace executed by an external coding agent, so the vision/LLM loop belongs to the caller and ai/authority are capped. The encoded loop transcribes scanned arcade schematics into a structured board graph with human-verifiable component/net records; agent skills identify components without inventing pinouts and a reviewer verifies/wires detections before export, so AI-produced detections feed persistent graph state with a human gate. Durable: structured graph, per-sheet .kicad_sch exports, reparsing and optional KiCad ERC; some ERC wiring unfinished.

Record's own backend composes specialized LLM workflows (paper-to-PPT with parallel consistent style, paper-to-draw.io) that turn a paper into diagrams/routes/plots/decks, so the model loop decides the generated structure. Mask-edit tests and committed editable PPTX fixtures evidence AI revision of produced decks, though targeted-region revision is weakly sourced. Articulation is multi-authority and durable: executable WorkflowCanvas graph, output-specific editors, HTML-to-editable-PPTX with ONLYOFFICE projection and inline Draw.io editor make continuing authoring editable rather than image-only.

Record's own multi-agent pipeline parses a paper into structured content/assets, plans a spatial hierarchy (tree_split_layout) and paints the poster; a critic loop sends visual defects back through a correction loop, so the AI makes layout/content decisions and iterates its own output. Mutation is real: generation-and-repair coordinates revision of the poster material, though the durable authority is the output .pptx. Parsed content/layout state is the planning authority; native PowerPoint objects and evaluation code make the loop inspectable.

Parametric CAD studio whose agent path is a typed MCP surface for an external model; the record itself does not call models (OpenCascade WASM kernel is deterministic), so ai_in_loop and authority are capped at 2. Mutation is strong: studio-agent-service stages agent document mutations with preview-before-commit on a schema-versioned document, and BRep evidence (topology + measured geometry) feeds back into the loop. Articulation: schema-5 parametric document with history and STEP/STL/DXF/project export is a durable editable authority beyond text-to-mesh.

CLI plus skill for an external coding agent: the bundled skill directs the agent while the CLI performs deterministic changes, and the design loop belongs to the calling model, so ai/authority are capped. Mutation: the AI drives report commands (create pages/visuals, apply themes, validate, package) against persistent PBIR/TMDL source files, giving structured mutating access through typed contracts rather than arbitrary JSON patching. Articulation: versionable PBIP/PBIR/TMDL source package with snapshots/restore is the authority; rendered .pbix is delivery material.

Ten-skill KiCad workspace executed by an external coding agent, so the model loop belongs to the caller and ai/authority are capped. The encoded loop generates KiCad source, runs independent checks (ERC/DRC/simulation), and can be blocked by mid-stage renders or human review, mutating project artifacts repeatedly across a full board lifecycle from topology to fab-ready release. Durable handoffs: STATUS.md, project folders with artifacts index, datasheets, analysis JSON, sourcing choices and timestamped release outputs; platform reach is honestly limited (macOS/KiCad 10 tested).

Closed file-native design system; design decisions are taken by external configured agents (Claude/Codex/Gemini) through the MCP/CLI while the product's own AI features (image generation, text AI via hosted providers) are not a core design loop, so ai/authority are penalized per closed-product rules. Mutation is strong and documented: execute/MCP design operations mutate the active .pen graph, with browser import, component/ref/descendant overrides and one-way Script conversion vs layers. Articulation: explicitly saved, Git-friendly JSON .pen document plus libraries/scripts/assets is the durable authority; no autosave, no semantic merge protocol.

Original vector-design runtime with an embedded agent: backend supplies schemas and reasoning while tool execution stays in the browser, so the record's own loop streams tool calls into a flat scene store. Batch design operations are grouped into one undo entry and transactional scene mutations edit the same store the renderer and user editing use, including a documented fix where agent-facing serialization had to match the rendered layout. Pixelless authority: scene store drives direct editing, rendering, agent reads/writes, undo and export; document persistence via documentStore and historyStore.

OpenPencil-derived product whose ordinary loop remains prompt or direct canvas editing, extending the same authority through MCP: connection and entity tools open/mutate/save the native document rather than returning detached suggestions, so agents (via the product's own prompt loop and MCP) take design decisions on screen connections, entities/fields/views. Mutations go through the same document store and history boundary as human edits. Articulation is the native .op document extended into a navigable storyboard and lightweight data model; attribution limited to a one-commit mirror with original repo 404.

Official Penpot behavior layer (skills + policies) executed by an external agent against the raw Penpot MCP, so the model loop belongs to the caller and ai/authority are capped. The layer encodes governed mutation: three authority modes (suggest-only, review-gated, small approved auto-fixes), with meaningful writes requiring preview image and summary before continuation. Articulation of the kit itself: shared pipeline/report schemas and golden evals are testable and durable, DESIGN.md and reports are downstream evidence artifacts, while Penpot's file (not the kit) keeps versioning/undo; kit is a read-only seed copied into user scope.

Record's own server calls Gemini to generate React/React Native projects; follow-up responses contain only changed files that the client merges by path into the current bundle, so the AI creates and then iteratively repairs existing source, with runtime errors surfaced as explicit correction requests against that current bundle. The saved multi-file project string in Firestore (per chat id) is the recoverable authority; WebContainer mounts a projection and ZIP/Netlify deliver the runtime filesystem. No source version graph: each follow-up overwrites saved current content, so earlier states depend on external history.

Figma plugin combining model generation with background removal, upscaling and image tracing; architecture-level evidence only — the creator discloses no model providers, transport, vectorization algorithm or licensing, and no current first-party changelog/source exists, so AI capabilities are asserted but only partly evidenced. Correction paths process the user's input into new artifacts rather than editing existing persistent design work. Tracing claims host-native vector layers (structurally different editability from generated bitmaps), but resolution/grouping/color-hole behavior is unknown.

Record's own chat loop translates intents into queued canvas actions with current selection and attachments as context, so the model takes design decisions for images/edits/HTML cards/ideation while humans continue with selection tools and direct manipulation. Mutation: AI actions apply to the active canvas with layer-aware context, though the dossier evidences action queuing more than deep iterative revision. Articulation: Postgres persists the tldraw canvas document + chat history, snapshot persistence hydrates the board from the tldraw snapshot (not the cover image), and the Fabric editor has its own serialization and undo history — all before derivative delivery (PNG/NFT/gallery).

The product is a first-party brand authority artifact prepared for agent consumption, not an agent: the repository contains no model call and takes no design decisions — AI is hypothetical here (capped). Enforcement depends on the consuming agent/reviewers since the system does not lint or write generated artifacts. Articulation is middling: canonical design-system Markdown beside approved assets is durable and Git-versioned, and generated pages/decks are reviewed against the same contract, but nothing AI-produced is persisted by the record itself.

Desktop agent with a dedicated Design mode whose bundled visual-design skill drives creation; the agent produces an HTML artifact that runs in a live runtime where the user can select elements and edit properties directly, then ask the agent to revise the same work — closing the edit-revise loop with the record's own agent. Rust artifact commands own filesystem/session persistence and reopen, so the artifact is the working authority and screenshots are previews. Articulation capped: no collaborative branch/version model evidenced; recoverability is at the local artifact/session level.

Record's own chat engine supplies prior messages to Gemini and requires complete HTML, making the assistant's full response the site artifact; a later correction sees earlier source as conversation history, so the AI regenerates/overwrites the site within chat. Mutation is real but coarse (whole-HTML replacement, no separate VFS snapshot). Articulation: Firestore retains authenticated chats and message ordering persistently and the preview is direct srcDoc, but there is no separate version entity or deployment record, capping durability.

Instruction package (skill) run inside Claude Code: the model loop that compares Figma reference screenshots against the running implementation belongs to the external agent, so ai/authority are capped per the critical rule. The encoded loop is a strong mutation loop: it preflights Figma MCP/Chrome, implements, captures runtime screenshot + computed styles, diagnoses visual difference and repeatedly corrects repository source until convergence; Figma stays reference authority and is never mutated. Repository source is the durable authority; screenshots are transient evidence; no independent metric engine or persisted comparison history.

The app itself does not call a model (stated explicitly): AI participation comes from a co-located external coding agent following the documented skill and command interface, so ai/authority are capped. Mutation: the external agent reads and writes the same structured design JSON that the human canvas edits; changes are structured, inspectable and immediately rendered, with demo mode exercising declared interactions. Articulation: design JSON is the meeting point (windows, elements, hierarchy, sizing, responsive visibility, actions), persisted in repo files, with HTML/JSON/XML exports deriving from the model rather than replacing it.

Collaborative native design file with MCP transports (local desktop / remote token) that hand design context to external IDE agents; the record's own Pixso AI generation exists at architecture level but its loop is not source-verified, and design decisions via agents come through the MCP contract, so ai/authority stay moderate. Mutation is absent from the evidenced tool contract: getCode/getImage return grounded HTML-shaped structure and rendered assets for implementation, and edit authority stays in the Pixso file (agents do not mutate it). Articulation: native file with pages/layers/components/styles/variables plus sharing permissions is durable.

General agent coworker whose design-relevant surface is a first-class artifacts view: agents in sessions produce HTML/PDF/Markdown/images/video/XMind/Excalidraw/Draw.io results that can be previewed, so model-driven creation happens inside the product's agent sessions. Authority is general-purpose rather than design-specialized. Mutation is bounded by design: published artifacts are shared read-only context with explicit database identity, ownership and API access — not a writable channel filesystem. Articulation: publication, runtime read tools and the artifact tree make persistence, collaboration and reuse explicit parts of the visual-output loop.

Record's own prompt-to-app loop: Inngest conversation tools let the model list/read/create/update/rename/delete file records in the Convex project graph, so the AI generates and then directly revises existing files; CodeMirror gives a parallel human source surface and WebContainer projects the current file tree for preview/terminal evidence. GitHub import/export is an explicit synchronization boundary with its own job lifecycle; the Convex project remains authoritative until a remote operation succeeds. Articulation capped by absence of a snapshot/restore ledger — in-product project is a latest-state authority, history only after export.

Visual automation platform composing agent/tool nodes into executable blueprints; the dossier evidences node history, connector validation, grouping, project state and flow execution, but no model call or AI design decision in the record itself — workflows are human-composed with AI agents as executed nodes, so ai/authority are capped. No evidence AI edits the persistent blueprint graph. Articulation: the canvas owns executable structure with project state and execution feedback, and routes/schedules/published project services are downstream forms of the same durable blueprint.

Language spec + parser with a posecode-mcp package that exposes generation/critique to external agents; the record itself contains no model call, so per the critical rule ai_in_loop and authority cap low. .posecode text source is the canonical durable, inspectable, diffable artifact, giving good articulation.

SVG-native multi-agent presentation workflow whose five roles (Planner/Designer/Reviewer etc.) drive model-driven deck creation from brief through to native-format slides. Natural-language edits resolve via slide manifest, target semantic SVG and save prior source under history before regeneration; Reviewer routes failures back to responsible roles. Semantic SVG + manifest own editability and persist as durable structured authority.

Presentation skill/workbench where staged docs feed deck_model.json as editable canvas source and a runnable workbench supports object selection/move/resize/inspector edits; HTML Direct Mode edits built decks with stable markers. The AI loop is executed by the host agent following the skill, so loop/authority are moderate; model contracts, manifests and the workbench give durable, editable articulation.

Deterministic converter.py pipeline that translates web DESIGN.md into presentation-image DESIGN.md + conversion manifest; the record makes no model call and performs no design creation (an image/slide agent consumes its output later). Output files are durable and editable, but the record itself has no AI loop, authority or mutation.

Agent skill with real scripts: locked design_spec → per-slide SVG → finalize/validate → DrawingML PPTX with delivery checks, so the host agent generates the full editable deck. Native PPTX geometry is the handoff authority with reproducible intermediates, but mutation is largely one-shot materialization; quick mode trades away the resumable staged workflow.

Real backend with content/template/image/design/document agents generating decks from a large template set and writing .pptx files. Direct SlideEditor exists but the global chat is not wired into it (App.jsx logs 'would integrate'), so AI-driven mutation of the open deck is not yet source-proven; deck history and native files give durable articulation.

DeepPresenter agent loop plans, authors per-slide HTML in a workspace, renders for visual reflection, and repairs defects before PPTX materialization; the record's own model-driven design loop is core. HTML slide files are the editable authority; conversation/tool state is persisted separately in JSONL.

Browser presentation editor whose AIPPT path streams an editable outline + typed slides that land directly in the normal editor slide store, then export to PPTX. Generation feeds the same editable authority, but two human checkpoints (outline, template) and no evidence of AI re-editing existing slides cap authority/mutation; IndexedDB snapshots give durable articulation.

Architecture-level capability-routing skill executed by an external host agent; no own model call or implementation source, so loop and authority are capped per the critical rule. Routing to editable PPTX/HTML authorities, media roles and visual QA give decent articulation despite the absence of runnable code.

Four real agents (Requirements/Journey/Wireframe/HighFidelity) transform a PRD into structured JSON specs, wireframes and a merged UI spec with exporters; models called for real in non-mock mode. Linear accumulation with no evidence of AI revising earlier stage outputs or visual validation caps mutation; stage artifacts and exports are durable.

Python component-tree framework whose GenerativeUI mode accepts model-written Prefab Python, validates it in browser/server sandboxes and serializes only what imports into a versioned PrefabApp JSON envelope rendered by a trusted React renderer. Model-authoring is constrained to the component vocabulary and persistence is delegated to the host, capping authority/mutation; the versioned envelope is a strong durable artifact.

Codex-compatible skill pack (SKILL.md + grid assets + SVG output rules) executed by the host agent; no model call in the record, so loop/authority stay low. Explicit construction grids, repair pass and audit/revision gates instruct the agent to fix malformed SVG, and editable SVG is a durable artifact authority.

Tool-calling code agent reconstructs a VirtualFileSystem from the project graph and performs file creation/replacement/rename/delete plus Figma tools during the streamed response; design libraries enter as agent context. AI directly mutates the persistent project authority. On completion the serialized file graph persists to PostgreSQL.

Outline-first slide app whose presentation agent can search, regenerate and edit an existing presentation, parsing generated XML into the same Plate-based slide graph as direct editing. Up to 50 undo/redo snapshots and Prisma-backed persistence make the managed slide graph a durable authority; PPTX export is best-effort/lossy.

Local web app where an agent session creates and revises stored HTML slides across turns; session.py persists sessions/messages/slide records on disk and the agent mutates that persisted state. PPTX is a projection of the ordered HTML slide state; the conversational UI is the main editing surface.

Repo-native studio for Claude Code: script + executable style-reference implementation → agent authors a self-contained HTML deck, revised through browser review or new instructions. Generation belongs to the host agent (loop/authority capped); HTML is both authority and delivery artifact, and revision operates on the persistent source file.

Self-hostable AI presentation workspace: brief/document → typed outline → typed presentation structure → editable Konva slide elements → PPTX/PDF with preserved editability. AI creates the full structured deck, but editing is human drag/inline work with no evidence of AI iterating existing decks; typed models and editor state give durable articulation.

Architecture-level closed deck engine behind browser editor, REST API and MCP: users describe a deck, then edit generated copy/layout/charts by chat or nudges, guided by a saved brand kit; exports to PPTX/PDF/Slides. Closed implementation with no published schema, exact tools or version graph penalizes articulation; chat-driven revision of the generated deck is evidenced.

Local-first studio where prompts/docs become a deck graph on a fixed canvas; direct manipulation shares the same element model as generation, and natural-language remix works at element/slide scope on existing decks. Undoable state and IndexedDB persistence make the deck graph a durable revision authority; exports are downstream materializations.

Specialist agent pipeline (planner/art-director/composer/choreographer/critic) with RAG converges on a validated Scene IR (palette, camera, lights, motion) and regenerate-scene replaces only a targeted scene with stable identity, revalidating the whole document. IR owns design intent and compiles to a Next.js project, but stays in client memory without a durable project DB or version graph.

Generator service (Ollama/OpenAI-compatible) produces typed diagram specs rendered by Mermaid/draw.io; artifact records live in the database with MinIO storage independent of any inference request. No evidenced AI mutation of stored specs or bidirectional sync back from draw.io caps mutation; artifacts are durable and separately editable.

Closed product with a partially shipped surface (token-bound demo components copied into Figma) while its broader agent generation is waitlisted and unpublished; token sharing between code/agents is claimed but not evidenced. Low scores for current-model-loop and AI mutation; the token model and exportable components are a durable-ish design-system authority.

Historical tutorial where DALL-E turns a prompt into a raster decal that the user applies to a fixed shirt scene with color/logo choices; the model call takes one bounded design decision. Scene state is runtime-only — the final canvas downloads but nothing persists as an editable project, and AI never edits existing work.

Client-side generator: prompt OpenAI for a target-specific file set, parse file blocks into Monaco tabs, preview web output and ZIP-download. Conversational context and regeneration can replace/add source, but files live in component state with no project database, durable version model or refresh recovery (browser-side API key too).

Figma-embedded assistant from Superun with bounded operations — Kick Start, Style Transfer, Region Design, Smart Fill, element modification, frame redesign — whose import step materializes native editable frames/Auto Layout/layers. Closed implementation leaves node-mapping and preservation mechanics undisclosed, but AI clearly modifies existing layout work and results land in the durable Figma file.

Local multi-model workspace whose canonical artifact is a typed UISchema tree; streaming generation accepts existing-project context and an optional focus node, enabling bounded mutation of an existing graph, and export walks the tree to static bundles. DB schema holds projects/screens/variants/prototypes/version snapshots with full-project restore — excellent durable articulation.

Streamlit app that calls Gemini Flash and parses one response into distinct HTML/CSS/JS channels retained in the session, previewed and downloadable separately. No correction or revision protocol — another prompt creates another session result — so mutation is nil and persistence beyond the session is absent.

Minimal prompt-to-HTML workspace: FastAPI sends the prompt to an OpenAI chat model under a frontend-only instruction and the returned string is shown as code plus iframe.srcdoc. No graph, patch protocol or server-side project record; a new prompt replaces the string and copy-to-clipboard is the only delivery path.

Closed product whose named agent loop clarifies constraints, plans parts, builds parametric geometry, renders multiple views, reads its geometry code, diagnoses defects and repeats the build; stable IDs derive part lists to exports (STEP/DXF/STL/etc.). Human sliders refine the same model; kernel, versioning and identifier survival across exports are undisclosed, capping articulation.

Backend asks OpenRouter for labeled HTML/CSS/JS blocks parsed into a structured response; authenticated projects store the three layers with a seven-day Mongo TTL and reassemble them for iframe preview and ZIP download. No intra-project snapshots or AI-driven revision path; storage is durable but deliberately expiring.

Claude streams a tagged artifact under a full-content replacement contract into a live workspace; model creates the React component. The model rewrites the artifact content (replacement), and manual edits are re-evaluated. Authority is real but session-scoped: no database, file export, version graph or reopen path.

Prompt-to-site and screenshot-to-site app with explicit demoMode provenance, optimization before/after pairs and up to 80 stored source versions; checkpoints compare and restore snapshots while appending restore records instead of erasing history. AI generates full sites and optimizes code; deployment is explicitly mocked, and durable Mongo project/version records give strong articulation.

Prompt-to-site builder that runs Cursor Composer with filesystem tools denied, parsing a <boltArtifact> program into a browser file graph reduced from ordered actions (later actions overwrite existing paths) and mounting it in WebContainer for preview. Refinement is overwrite history in component state; the only durable exit is a client-generated ZIP, and the code pane is read-only.

Streams Gemini component source into an isolated script-enabled iframe and saves history only after completed responses; completed generations become selectable browser-local versions in localStorage. AI writes full component source but does not edit previous versions, and persistence is localStorage-scoped with no reopen/export path.

Two-repo Lovable-style builder where Spring AI tools perform explicit file reads/writes on a server-owned project file set, chat and tool events persist separately, and the browser streams file events to reload server-owned content; Kubernetes runner gives a six-hour preview. AI mutation is the core loop and files are durable, but preview is expiring and no version-restore ledger exists.

Generated React/Tailwind source with three mutation paths — another Gemini prompt, direct Monaco editing, and restoring local prompt history — plus scoring, copy and React/HTML export. AI regeneration is replacement-style, and the store is client-side with no server project database or durable versioning.

Deliberately small browser-only loop: OpenRouter returns a GeneratedComponent string kept in memory for regeneration, template prompts and download; a lossy sanitizer preview strips JSX expressions. The code panel preserves more authority than the preview, but nothing persists beyond the current browser session and AI never edits existing work.

Standards-first platform where AI architects operate on persisted React-Flow node/edge canvases and a presentation agent reads all project surfaces into an append-only blackboard, builds an exact slide skeleton and checkpoints slide JSON as content/images arrive. Persisted Supabase graph plus checkpointed, directly editable slide JSON and multi-format delivery give excellent durable articulation.

Agent-agnostic visual verification CLI: start-test-stop sessions record video, screenshots, timing, errors and reports that attach to PRs, while an external agent drives the browser. The record contains no model call, creates no design and never mutates the application (Git/app stay authoritative); its evidence bundles are durable but are verification artifacts, not designed output.

Skill suite (proto-me, open-canvas, plan) executed by a host Codex agent: the interactive canvas exposes the brief as editable nodes, refreshes update text in place preserving layout, and generated visuals are annotated communication assets while proto-plan writes the accepted brief to a durable execution handoff. Design is optional and references never outrank the confirmed brief.

React visual-editor kernel with no model call and no first-party agent interface in core: host application defines config/data and persists via onPublish, while humans drag/field-edit a structured Data object (root/content/zones with stable IDs and migration support). The durable data model and editor are excellent primitives, but the record itself contains no AI loop, creation or mutation.

Bridge stack (MCP server + WebSocket hub + Figma plugin) that lets an external agent (Cursor) execute native Figma operations like rectangle/text creation, batch text replacement and connectors; reasoning belongs to that external agent, so loop and authority are capped per the critical rule. The mechanism does enable real AI-driven mutation of the durable native Figma document.

Closed QoderWork design workbench: agent writes engineering files (HTML-first or React-library targets) into an optional local Working Folder behind Canvas/Design Files/Preview, with planning contract, lasso/annotation, Nudge parameters and handoff to Qoder IDE. Strong agent-authored loop with file-based mutation, but closed implementation leaves .design.json schema, Nudge write path, Canvas serialization and versioning undisclosed, capping articulation.
