Constrained write: new artifact creation only, no in-place mutation of existing work.

Live Blender automation with 93 modeled tools including architectural operations; a visual studio supports record/replay of sessions and portable, editable session.json files make an agent run inspectable and replayable. Structural scene-graph mutation across many tool domains with a session/replay layer that makes runs reversible and repeatable.

Single-file Blender add-on exposing modeling, materials, animation, physics, render and interchange operations to orchestrating agents, with thread-safe queuing onto Blender's main thread. Broad structural scene-graph mutation over native Blender objects; no session/undo layer beyond Blender and the saved .blend.

26 tools over Blender's Lab MCP extension (TCP 9876) that inspect scene state, apply focused Python or tool-level mutations, then verify via object measurements, screenshots or saved renders before export. Structural scene mutation with an inspect-mutate-verify loop; no durable agent-session or undo semantics beyond Blender and the saved file.

Socket bridge where a Python MCP server translates tool calls for an installed Blender add-on that executes Blender Python against the live scene; agents can create, modify, inspect, render and export objects and scenes, and users can continue ordinary editing after agent operations. Deep structural mutation of the native scene graph plus export delivery.

The original running-scene bridge: scene inspection, viewport screenshots, object creation and deletion, material changes and an unrestricted Python escape hatch into the live Blender dependency graph and API. Structural scene-graph operations plus arbitrary Python close the full-authoring surface, with screenshots closing an inspect-correct-inspect loop; safety and save discipline remain with the user.

Rendering bridge covering roughly 27 diagram syntaxes via Kroki: agents submit diagram source, invoke render tools, and receive inline previews to iterate in the coding environment. Diagram source files remain authoritative and the preview is a derived image; no native canvas, object-level collaboration or reversible graph operations. Constrained write: create/render diagram artifacts, no structural mutation of an existing graph.

Compile-time DOM-to-source bridge plus hosted AI turns: selection yields exact file/line/column, agents run with the project as working directory (Claude defaults to bypass permissions), and a guarded Revert writes provider-derived inverse edits back into project files with project-root containment and current-content matching. Deep repository-file mutation with evidence of guarded undo; no design artifact graph of its own.

Cloud mode owns saved-workflow lifecycle: submit a custom workflow, save it to the account, update it with a recoverable version, share it or open it on the Comfy Cloud canvas for human correction; local mode is a comfy-cli-driven adapter for discovery, validation and execution against a user-owned installation. Workflow-graph artifacts are versioned and bidirectional with the canvas, but the cloud server is closed (architecture-level) and local mode is mostly an execution adapter.

ComfyUI node suite combining content-aware analysis with grading controls that produce images inside the authoritative workflow graph; auto/preset/manual modes are parameter-driven and human-tuned. It is a processing node rather than an agent-facing bridge: an external agent can only invoke deterministic color operations or set parameters, with no in-place structural mutation of artwork.

Local-first control plane whose agent inspects the node vocabulary of a running ComfyUI install, authors and edits the workflow graph, executes it, diagnoses failures and continues the same session; a workflow-target store pins the graph per tab and fails closed on canvas changes, node snapshots back recoverable infrastructure changes, and save warnings protect unsaved work. Structural node-graph authoring/editing with session continuity.

Runtime-intent relay: the overlay captures selection, layout, sketch and bug evidence (logs, console, DOM snapshots, events) and MCP tools hand it to a coding agent that edits the real React/Angular/Tailwind source, verified by reloading the app. The bridge owns evidence packaging and intent commit but not the source mutation or its undo; repository remains final authority.

Browser visual editor emits structured edit events (URL, viewport, element path, before/after values, React/source context) that a local MCP-compatible agent writes into real project files; tasks are the unit of concurrency and can be reverted independently (browser effect and source change both rolled back) with a per-element session undo stack. Deep source-file mutation with task-level revert per first-party contract; implementation is closed, so details stay architecture-level.

Standalone Computer-Use runtime for hosts without a typed API: each action is tied to a concrete PID and window plus a fresh observation ID, and a new observation is required after a mutation; physical Escape, visible control indicators and sensitive-window policy stay in the Host process. Capability is constrained GUI-level input (clicks/keystrokes re-verified by observation) rather than typed structural operations.

Typed 3ds Max host adapter: separately declared Skills for modeling, mesh topology, materials, cameras/lights, animation, rigging, display, import/export and rendering, with scene-changing operations returned to the application's main thread and material creation/bitmap binding mutating real host objects. Broad structural scene mutation; no undo-manager integration evidenced.

Typed AEP surface over the adobepy broker/CEP bridge: project Skill opens/saves, imports assets and creates compositions; layer tools cover text, transforms, masks, effects, ordering and keyframes; render tools queue and configure the native render queue. Full motion-design lifecycle creation and deep layer/keyframe iteration, with raw ExtendScript kept as an explicitly destructive fallback.

Blender host adapter embedding a Streamable HTTP server with typed, progressively loadable skills across scene assembly, mesh/UV, rigging, materials, node graphs, physics, rendering and interchange; calls serialize onto Blender's UI thread and context snapshots bound agent perception. Broad structural scene-graph and node-graph mutation; no undo/replay layer beyond the host.

Headless c4dpy adapter stages a native C4D document in an isolated worker, runs inspection, validation and modeling operations on the staged copy, and atomically promotes the result to the durable .c4d only on success; renders bounded previews and exports C4D/OBJ/FBX/glTF/STL/Alembic/Collada. Complete document creation and full modeling with transactional, failure-safe promotion.

ComfyUI workflow as a validated asynchronous job: endpoints validate graph structure, submit over REST/WebSocket returning job identity, query status and retrieve artifacts tied to the run; changing nodes or parameters produces new comparable graph executions. The adapter keeps the native workflow JSON as the editable recipe and avoids a hidden generation state, but graph authoring depth is submission-oriented rather than in-place structural editing.

Creative-tool control plane: a gateway indexes live DCC instances and progressively exposes search, describe, load and call operations plus async jobs, cancellation, workflow checkpoints, artifacts, audit and policy, with an Admin UI for traces/logs/statistics. Mutation capability flows through host adapters, but via one bounded contract an AI can discover and operate many hosts and checkpoint workflows; it explicitly cannot guarantee rollback for arbitrary host APIs.

Agent-facing adapter for Autodesk Flow Production Tracking: entity CRUD (create and update the same shots/assets/versions artists see), notes carrying review decisions back into the graph, search, schema discovery and batches. This is constrained write on a production-tracking database (object creation and field/status updates), not structural mutation of a design artifact.

Headless parametric-CAD adapter: session tools create, inspect and validate the native .FCStd document, modeling runs in FreeCAD's Python runtime with the dependency graph recomputed, and the staged document is accepted only when invariants hold; edits are dependency-aware and failures leave original bytes unchanged. Structural feature/dependency-graph mutation with transactional safety.

Packaged EditorPlugin, debugger bridge and sidecar exposing 163 typed tools by domain (scene, UI, animation, audio, navigation, tile, resource) that run on the editor thread, use Godot's undo manager where the host supports it, restrict paths to res://, and separate in-memory scene change from explicit save/validation. Deep scene/resource-graph mutation with host undo integration.

Embedded agent-facing server mapping typed Skills onto the procedural node network across scene assembly, SOP/DOP/LOP/CHOP, materials, animation, cameras, rendering and pipeline jobs; agents read bounded graph state first, mutations dispatch to the host thread, and atomic node-chain builders expose procedural structure as native nodes. Deep structural node-graph authoring with long jobs kept queryable.

Typed vector-document layer over the adobepy broker: document tools inspect artboards, layers, selections, placed/raster items, text, stories and swatches; artwork tools update text and path points and apply translation/scale/rotation; export Skill saves AI/PDF/EPS and exports PNG/JPEG/SVG. Structural edits of vector artwork with session-scoped object identity.

Production texture/lookdev adapter: a Qt-timer plugin executes bounded Mari API commands on the GUI thread while an external sidecar owns networking and jobs; surface follows project lifecycle, geometry/channels, node graph and layers, shaders, images and texture export, including create_node/create_layer on the native graph. Structural node-graph/layer mutation with main-thread safety; saved Mari project is authoritative.

Toolbag lookdev/validation adapter: the scene Skill imports FBX, assigns explicit PBR maps, frames objects, finds missing references, saves the scene and renders camera images as asynchronous jobs around Toolbag's native calls, requiring job/state inspection rather than blind re-issue. Scene and material mutation plus render loop, but narrower than a full authoring surface.

Broad Maya host product: a Rust sidecar and gateway with a Qt dispatcher progressively expose more than seventy typed operations across scene, mesh, UV, material, rig, animation, simulation, rendering and pipeline work, producing ordinary DAG/DG/Bifrost/material/animation/render structures; long work can be cancelled or recovered by job identity and save state is explicit. Full-scope structural scene mutation across artifact domains.

Typed Skill package for AdvancedSkeleton rigging: inspects installed presets, imports or creates a FitSkeleton, configures labels, orientation, twist/bendy, follow and controller attributes, and supports both Build and ReBuild so a rig can be reconstructed from the fit structure rather than remaining a one-shot result. Structural rig construction with a reproducible build/rebuild loop.

Marketplace Skill for mGear Shifter rigging: inspects the environment and components, creates a guide from a named template, builds a rig from it, exports the guide as a reusable template, and imports rigs through an AssetDescriptor contract. Rig build lifecycle centered on a reproducible guide authority; narrower than a general scene-authoring surface.

Domain Skill generating residential exterior concepts in Maya/Bifrost/Arnold: six styles, seeded variation, material roles and a staged review orbit, producing material-separated Bifrost structural graphs and instanced details with generated parts capped, prototypes reused by role and partial nodes removed after error or cancellation. Generates and corrects structural scene graphs with deterministic variation.

Constrained compositing and reusable-node workflow: layered-compositing Skill applies ordered gain, saturation, edge-feather and albedo-fill adjustments globally or through Cryptomatte selection, materializing results through an explicit Write node; node-assets Skill packages versioned Gizmos with bounded public knobs, instantiates and validates them. Structural node-graph and component-lifecycle operations in Nuke.

Deterministic adapter for inspection, validation, parameterized rendering and geometry export: it parses modules/functions/variables without executing source, accepts only JSON scalar/array parameters (no raw -D expressions), stages outputs next to destinations with visible-on-success semantics, requires explicit overwrite, and links each artifact by SHA-256. Constrained write: parameter-driven renders/exports of an existing .scad authority; it deliberately does not write arbitrary source.

Headless USD authoring/validation product: both USDA-text and pxr modes create projects and stages, list and define prims, set transforms, add references, snapshot and validate; material binding, cameras/lights, time-sampled animation, sublayers, payloads and variants run through pxr, and a validation package can create USDZ archives. Structural USD scene-graph compositing and mutation with explicit mode reporting.

Typed Photoshop product over the adobepy Rust broker and UXP bridge: creates/opens documents, inspects the layer stack, creates/deletes layers, changes opacity/visibility/blend mode, edits text, makes selections, applies filters and works with smart objects, preserving the editable PSD graph before save/export. Complete layered-document lifecycle with structural layer-graph mutation.

Controls official RenderDoc capture paths (launch/attach/delayed capture) and converts .rdc frames into reviewable evidence artifacts, but explicitly does not mutate the source game or scene; writes are creation of bounded new capture/export files only.

Embeds a server in Designer's Qt main thread and can inspect the active session and create one rendered procedural PBR material package through the native session; surface is bounded one-pass material creation, no editing of existing graphs.

Mutates the native layer stack of the authoritative .spp project: creates PBR fill/textured layers, searches resources and applies smart materials via resource URLs; structural layer-tree work bounded to a material-authoring pass.

Full operator-network access: traverse operators, read/write parameters, save/load .toe/.tox state, capture viewport, plus typed operations and optional Python execution (td native automation); limited undo reported as a host boundary.
Writes durable .tracy capture and computed CSV summaries via official Tracy binaries and validates extensions; analysis and capture only, no mutation of the instrumented host or its design content.

Deep mutation across the Unity project graph: scene operations create GameObjects and change transforms through Unity Undo before explicit save, allowlisted CAS source-asset writes, compilation/Play Mode, tests and Windows player builds — near-complete lifecycle.

Complete authoring surface over Unreal 4.18+: actors, assets, Blueprints, levels, materials, cinematics, Niagara, MetaSound, Chaos, gameplay tests and packaging, composing with Epic's native MCP toolsets; skills declare affinity/mutability/destructiveness.

Authors the native interactive-audio graph via WAAPI: import segments, build Random/Sequence/Switch containers, create events, set properties/references and configure RTPC curves, with SoundBank generation and Work Unit persistence; no arbitrary scripting.

Mutates the selected native subtool (refine/remesh/bake) plus selection, OBJ export and turntable capture through the ZBrush Python SDK; pre-alpha with busy-state recovery and a narrower, less-verified surface.

Selector-bound value sets, widget clicks and QAction triggering with event-loop processing and screenshot return for legacy PySide/PyQt hosts; property/parameter-level correction layer, no structural graph operations.

Orchestration and handoff layer coordinating Figma/Webflow/Shopify specialists with persisted templates and structured handoffs; actual host mutations are delegated to each service's MCP workspace, so the record's own write depth is coordination and contract files.

Reversible DOM/style mutations over the live page with per-change inverse records (style/DOM/text, move/insert/delete), undo, replay after reload and an MCP change lifecycle; session-scoped — durable source persistence happens only after external agent applies changes.
Read-only runtime verification: computed rectangles, CSS JSON, screenshots and ghost overlay measurement; never writes application code or mutates the page or repository.

Realpath-guarded source-file writes through the built-in CodeMirror editor plus rich runtime inspection/selection; the primary agent path reduces to plain-text prompting into an external CLI PTY, so writes are file-level and bounded to existing project files.

Structured generators materialize editable draw.io XML (RF signal chains with auto-layout/Friis math, PCB stack-ups, EMC setups) and redline screenshots; structural diagram creation on the native draw.io graph.
Two-way sync relays model-produced XML mutations into the live draw.io canvas via Monaco; structural diagram editing on the document format, though concurrent-edit merge safety is not established.

Official interface: inline MCP App, browser-opening tool server and coding-agent plugins all converge on editable draw.io XML; auto-layout and edge routing modify the graph, plugins write .drawio files and export PNG/SVG/PDF with embedded XML.

Broad native authoring across Figma, FigJam and Slides via Desktop Bridge plugin plus REST: create/modify frames, nodes, components, variables, FigJam objects and Slides content, with bidirectional DTCG token sync and explicit multi-file execution.

Structural node operations on live open files — geometry/appearance, text, fills/effects/strokes, auto-layout, shapes, grouping/reparenting, deletion with confirmation — while component/instance and variable/style authoring are deliberately out of scope.

Figma's official hosted contract is bidirectional full authoring: create_new_file, native Design generation, FigJam diagrams, Slides and library creation, plus editor skills executing bounded Plugin API code over frames, components, variables and auto-layout.

24 typed operation families from basic nodes through components, variables, vectors, annotations and export, dispatched via WebSocket to a plugin operation router against the native Figma graph; pre-release with mock/unit test evidence only.

Plugin-hosted figma_write runs bounded JavaScript creating/changing native nodes, frames, components and variables with per-file sessionId targeting; read/write separation and token handlers keep results in Figma's graph.

Multi-agent workflow builds Webflow site structure from Figma under Finsweet conventions in small MCP chunks with structured workspace files and an explicit approval gate before host mutation; durable design-system/page records are persisted in the workspace.

Approved repairs mutate the live native graph: token fixers bind variables, rename layers and update properties through the plugin runtime after audit findings; token-system and layer-structure fixes, user-approved with local session-state restore.
Deliberately narrow: simplified Figma data extraction and validated local image downloads only; no Figma mutation surface at all, no reverse sync.

Validated FusionActions (boxes, cylinders, holes, extrudes, fillets, materials) are executed by the local add-in against the native parametric document, mutating the feature tree; vocabulary explicitly bounded, not full Fusion automation.

Conversational create/modify/enhance on the live diagram: model responses are interpreted as draw.io XML mutations and subsequent prompts revise the same document; MCP edge lets external agents join the workflow.
Renders Mermaid fences in agent responses to terminal/PNG and preserves copy-source; no named project record, version history or mutation of persistent design content.

Temporary runtime DOM property edits on the live app captured as structured feedback packets through a live MCP session; durable writer is the external coding agent, and the extension itself does not change repository source.

Browser-injected visual changes can be staged, mapped and committed back into repository source via live-commit-manual-edits with explicit discard/recovery; deterministic detectors run without an LLM while the product brief persists.

Visual editing surface translates inline text edits and element moves into source changes on the local project with element-to-source mapping; broader intent delegated to connected coding agents, and closed implementation limits independent verification.

Persists element-aware annotations and PNG screenshots and exposes MCP tools that enumerate and mark findings resolved; the designed app itself is not mutated — repairs are carried out by the coding agent.

Sketch inspection/editing, FeatureScript operations and feature mutations on the native Onshape document, with multi-view renders, measurements and geometric diff returning observable truth for verification.
Read-mostly: parses native KiCad artifacts, calls kicad-cli for BOM/netlist/DRC/validation, records DRC history and exports evidence; no mutation of the board or project.

Permissioned progression from read-only review to controlled write/manufacturing modes with progressive disclosure; ERC/DRC and exports invoke KiCad engines, native files remain authoritative, and release is human-gated.

Registry-driven operations create/inspect schematics and boards, route, apply design rules and export manufacturing files against native KiCad artifacts; full engineering-authoring surface, not just image generation.
Snapshot-bounded constrained edits with post-mutation diff and evidence, delegating format/rule validation to KiCad; a guarded iteration loop deliberately narrower than full autonomous PCB authoring.

Generates and refines versioned Lottie/dotLottie state machines with schema/state-machine validation and deterministic auto-fix, writing versioned successors and exporting MP4/WebM/GIF; drives an external model subscription rather than containing the model loop itself.

Source annotations compile into a manifest that constrains edits; per-annotation revisions record author/channel and support rollback, enabling governed content changes to annotated regions; CLI/runtime sidecar incomplete so the user-facing surface is not delivered.

Browser-extension bridge relays structured diagram operations into the live diagrams.net editor, mutating the native graph without a shadow database; ordinary Draw.io save/export remains the persistence boundary.

80+ typed atomic modeling tools and 22 skills against native Autodesk Inventor documents with persistent entity tags for stable resolution; provider protocol separates generic semantics from host automation, SolidWorks planned only.

Agent creates/modifies the native CST project: parametric templates compute geometry from target frequency, then tools configure materials, ports, mesh and solvers, extract results and run sweeps/optimization; offline VBA plan mode supplements live native execution. Deep structural + optimization mutation of the host CAD/simulation project, though not a multi-artifact full authoring surface.

Live canvas server owns element/snapshot/file maps; CLI/MCP/REST mutate the scene graph with granular create/update/delete, batch ops, align/distribute/group and snapshot restore, and browser direct edits sync the full native scene back to the server. Bidirectional and structural, but authority is process-memory with no durable versioning/undo and a single artifact type.

Agent inspects Fusion's API, loaded add-ins and docs, then executes Python against the live native session; documented patterns create constrained sketches, extrusions and arbitrary Fusion API sequences in the parametric document while Fusion keeps dependencies, save files and undo history. Generic execution opens the complete native authoring surface.

The agent works at intent level — synthesizing filters, placing transmission zeros, meeting emissions constraints — importing/exporting LTspice ASC, SPICE and Qucs files into a circuit IR, and driving model-aware optimization against independent simulators with durable job artifacts. Structural netlist/IR mutation with a design-simulate-revise chain, stopping before schematic-to-layout closure.

Typed geometry/frequency inputs become NEC decks; agent creates parameterized dipole, inverted-V, Yagi, vertical and loop models, invokes the solver, parses impedance/radiation results and revises. Constrained parameterized creation plus revision of model files with simulation evidence in the loop; mutation surface is narrow.

Server validates inputs and generates reproducible Python/openEMS solver scripts with explicit geometry, mesh, boundary and sweep parameters, runs the deterministic engine and returns artifacts; agent varies a parameter and reruns. Parameterized creation and parameter revision of generated jobs, output files remain inspectable authority.

Parses KiCad schematic/layout and BOM, cross-references constraints and produces shared findings, queuing deeper simulations when needed; the KiCad artifacts stay the review authority and are not structurally edited. Host mutation is limited to writing reports/queues — design files remain read-side input.

Bundled Draw.io server emits diagram events and XML and a local bridge connects to the packaged diagrams.net app; a real Cisco DevNet .drawio topology artifact is generated from pyATS-discovered device/topology facts and stays human-editable. Constrained creation of the editable topology document from live network data; the pyATS side is discovery/read.

Figma plugin pushes selected node data/pixels to a user-controlled n8n/REST workflow; the return path accepts direct commands that can modify the native Figma canvas, demonstrated in creator material. Native mutation capability exists, but transport is generic webhook and command validation/depth is undocumented.

Intentionally read-only: fetches Penpot data, validates against committed schemas, caches a normalized tree and provides screenshots/exports; no write tool exists at the reviewed revision. Fetch/parse/inspect only.

Agent inspects, creates and updates n8n workflow JSON (nodes, connections, settings) through typed SDK schemas, toggles activation and triggers execution; n8n remains the artifact authority. Structural workflow-graph mutation plus full workflow lifecycle (create/update/activate/execute).

Natural language compiles into a YAML CSpec that is resolved and linted against token/component registries into a scene graph, then emitted as constrained Figma Plugin API code executed against the native graph; fix recompiles from bounded corrections and done archives specs/snapshots/history. Deep, traceable native authoring; host Figma history governs versioning.

Model output is relayed into current draw.io XML changes and loaded into the embedded full editor where users keep ordinary object-level editing; PNG/.drawio/Mermaid exports serve delivery. Structural edits to an established XML canvas with human continuation, but the browser session holds state and there is no durable repo/versioning of its own.

Single custom server creates/reads/edits PPTX, composes raster images, synthesizes SVG and charts, drives GIMP/Inkscape and Blender/FreeCAD scripts, and creates Godot projects, with committed artifact-level test evidence. Broad multi-format structural mutation, each native format kept as its own authority.

Typed tools address live cloud documents directly: documents, Part Studios, sketches, constraints, features (extrude/revolve/fillet/pattern/mates), assemblies, variables, measurements, interference analysis and export via validated builders; native history/workspace semantics remain the version boundary. Full CAD authoring surface.

Annotations and reports on arbitrary web UIs are persisted in a local store with CRUD, metadata transitions and multi-fidelity report generation; the target page is deliberately untouched. Constrained write to the annotation store only — no mutation of the host design/application.

Agents create files/pages, write shapes, manage components/libraries/tokens, address comments and collaboration state and export host-rendered artifacts through the native HTTP API with batch and session-revision concurrency; snapshot tools are revision-aware. Deep structural mutation of the native file graph; destructive deletes gated by the caller.

Visible React Flow graph is narrowly configurable: Run rebuilds a payload with only the fixed query/LLM nodes and empty edges, and the backend makes one model call and writes a chat log. Host access is effectively one executed request; topology is not traversed or mutated.

Review sessions, annotations, approvals and approved-plan history persist locally; diff review can stage/unstage files and synchronized hooks translate approval/denial back into the agent workflow. Constrained mutation of review state plus git staging; the authoritative design artifacts remain the agent's own work.

Read-write local HTTP API into a development Figma plugin creates frames, text, components and instances and binds properties to design variables so token meaning survives; host version history is the recovery mechanism. Deep native graph mutation with semantic variable binding; closed implementation limits verification of completeness/transactions.

Bidirectional route: live Figma or rendered web normalizes into a Design Spec/semantic graph, agents emit React and run render/verify/fix correction passes; the design DSL runs in reverse to author native Figma nodes. Deep structural graph work plus verification-driven iteration across design and code authorities with cache recovery.

Agent-supplied JavaScript executes against a validated, guarded figma.* proxy that creates/mutates native nodes, variables and styles with layout math, paint and token guards, leader-elected plugin sessions preventing multi-window conflicts; structured audit plus screenshot close the loop. Deep native mutation with enforced policy.

AI-facing MCP tools are pull/read (selection, pending/formatted changes, comments, status) plus local-state clear; DOM/style/structure mutations are performed by the human overlay as a temporary runtime projection, and durable source edits are delegated to an external agent. Through the bridge the AI receives intent and clears local state, not host mutation.

Blocking MCP call and Cursor extension surface a review exchange where a person responds with text, voice or images and explicitly releases with TASK_COMPLETE; it relays visual intent back into the same agent turn and owns the review coordination, not the designed application. No structural mutation of the host artifact.

218 tools mutate the live Blender scene across mesh editing, geometry nodes, materials, animation, simulation and rendering; a self-refinement session renders multiple angles, sends viewport evidence to a local vision model and records successive scores and changes. Complete 3D authoring surface with an iterative repair loop.

Bridge exposes status, canvas inspection, definition load/solve/save, component creation, wiring, deletion, movement, values and code execution over a TCP host listener, plus a persistent layout learner that clusters and suggests readable placement. Deep structural mutation of the Grasshopper component graph; .gh/.ghx remains the durable definition.

Agent creates and modifies objects, operates layers and selection, inspects scene metadata, captures the viewport and executes Rhino Python against the live document; Rhino's native document, layer model and geometry kernel stay authoritative. Deep NURBS/scene mutation with code-execution breadth.

Agent mutates .scad source and exposed parameters directly through WebMCP tools in the shared TanStack store; OpenSCAD WASM auto-renders and reports duration, triangle count and failures before export. Complete editable loop on the program artifact, single format.

Structured diagram model maps agent requests into Draw.io XML with committed Basic/Azure shape identifiers, batch and layer operations, and transactional mode that stages a coherent edit set and commits or abandons it as a unit. Deep graph creation with transaction semantics; output is an editable handoff file rather than a live host.

The server opens a drag-and-drop Mermaid editor as an MCP interaction where the human moves nodes, edits labels and draws connections against a live preview; submitting returns corrected Mermaid to the agent. Editor mutation is human-driven and the loop is a runtime relay, not a durable diagram repository.

Five tools (create, iterate, extract, list, gallery) return structured execution specs; the IDE model writes HTML/SVG files under design_iterations/ and the gallery auto-discovers and renders them for comparison. Constrained creation and directory-level iteration of design artifacts; no hidden canvas or managed database, and generation is credited to the external model.

Plugin reads native Figma variables and can generate and write WEB custom-property code syntax back into the Figma file, then streams values into runtimes as injected CSS custom properties for live validation; promotion to repository source requires explicit human CSS export. Constrained token-level writes plus runtime projection; AI lacks independent promotion authority.

MCP tools surface selection, visual context, pending/formatted changes, comments, status, watch and clear; actual DOM/style/text/structure manipulation is the human overlay's temporary runtime layer (Shadow-DOM isolated), and source persistence is delegated to the coding agent. The AI receives intent over the bridge rather than executing host mutation.

Live mode inspects and mutates the open Resolve project — media pools, timelines, markers, LUTs and render jobs — through the scripting API with dry-run plans and confirmation, backed by deterministic engines (beat grid, color transforms, dialogue keep ranges, loudness); interchange artifacts (FCPXML/EDL/LUT) cover the offline path. Deep editing-project mutation with safety gates.

A central server coordinates one MCP surface routing host-specific operations to an extended Blender add-on and an Unreal plugin, operating two native scene authorities — the .blend scene and the Unreal project/level graph — without a merged intermediate format. Deep structural mutation on both 3D hosts.

Editor-embedded local HTTP MCP server executes native operations — spawning actors, configuring lighting, creating material instances, inspecting Slate widgets, running automation tests — synchronized serially onto the Unreal game thread, with a Toolset Registry for Python/C++ toolsets. Deep scene/asset mutation; evidence is Epic documentation (architecture-level), so details beyond the documented surface are unverified.

Three tools (pages info, data, images) inspect and render local Vextra/Figma/Sketch/SVG files for structural and visual grounding; explicitly read-only with no mutation of the source design file. Fetch/parse/inspect and render derivatives only.

Persistent local/SSH sessions expose Python and SKILL operations that read and mutate Cadence objects; examples cover stepwise schematic creation, connectivity inspection, parameter edits, Maestro sweeps and GDS export, with schematics/layouts/Simulation results remaining authority. Deep, domain-structured EDA mutation; licensed Cadence/PDK prevents public reproducibility.

MCP tools create and mutate typed ERD/BPMN/system-landscape models with atomic writes and layout sidecars while file watchers ingest outside edits; the React Flow/ELK editor returns structural changes to the store and persisted model. Bidirectional structural mutation of durable model files.

Fifteen action-grouped tools inspect, generate, push, audit and refactor pages, instances, styles, tokens, variables, resources and assets on the Webstudio Cloud graph behind two-stage dryRun→forceConfirmed mutations, plus read-only snapshots and audits for correction passes. Deep, broad mutation of the host project graph; reach rides a captured cookie/CSRF session and is not an official API.
